title: Edge0-145B Automation: How to Set It Up (2026 Guide)
summary: Edge0-145b automation reaches its first constraint at 256K tokens, so you can design long-running workflows that work with the documented interface.
body_markdown:
## Two ways to reach edge0-145b


Edge0-145b ships as open weights, not as an account on a hosted service. That means there are two real routes to a working call, and the six steps below read differently on each.


> A run that works on a short test input and fails on a real 300K-token export hasn't been automated, only demonstrated.


### Self-hosting edge0-145b with a local inference server


Download a quantised file from the[Hugging Face model page](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Edge0-145B-q3k) and serve it with a local inference server such as llama.cpp's` llama-server` or vLLM.


Either one exposes an HTTP endpoint, and most speak the OpenAI-style chat format, so the rest of your automation sees an ordinary URL.


On this route, access is a file download, and a credential exists only if you set one yourself, for example with the server's API-key option.


Hardware sizing and out-of-memory on load are fully yours: pick the file that fits your VRAM before you start, because a model that doesn't fit fails at load, not at the first request.


An Activepieces HTTP step against such a server looks like this. Use method POST, the URL` http://your-server:8080/v1/chat/completions` , a` Content-Type: application/json` header, and an` Authorization: Bearer` header if you set a key. The body is JSON with a` messages` array holding your prompt.


The server must be reachable from wherever Activepieces runs, since a cloud-hosted flow can't see your` localhost` .


### Using a third-party host for edge0-145b


If a provider hosts edge0-145b, you get a vendor-style endpoint with an account and a key, and the access and credential steps apply as written, including any approval queue.


I found no such host in the ModelRigs listing, so confirm one exists and read its documentation before planning around it.


Here hardware sizing and load-time out-of-memory drop out of your hands, but the host's own context, rate and timeout limits take their place. Those limits are the ones to write down in each step.
